subject: Post-call: unit price parity review and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: unit price parity review and next steps

Alex — thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we have a clean runbook for procurement: 

1) Volume profile you shared (high-level):
   - Pilot: ~25M tokens / mo for 3 months
   - Production target: ramp to 600M tokens / mo in Q4 (peak expected Q1 next year)

2) Budget and target unit economics:
   - Procurement budget band: $45k–$65k / mo during pilot (flexible)
   - Finance indicated target cost of goods goal ~ $7–$12 per 1M tokens at scale (they asked us to validate feasibility)

3) Redwood action items (what we committed to):
   - Run a short benchmarking sweep vs the host set you called out (OpenAI, Anthropic, and two open-hosts we see in your stack).
   - Produce a per-1M token parity sheet showing list price, likely negotiated floor, and expected delivery SLA tiers.
   - Provide a recommended target we think is realistic for production (given the volume distribution) and an example pricing cadence for pilot -> prod.

Attachments: I attached the volume estimates you shared (finlytics-volume-estimates.xlsx) and our internal host comparison template (redwood-host-comps-20270429.pdf).

Initial benchmarking notes (high level):
   - OpenAI gpt-4-style endpoints: list ~ $40–$50 / 1M (varies by context/window); effective negotiated floors often remain north of $20 / 1M for pilot-sized contracts.
   - Anthropic large chat model: list ~ $30–$45 / 1M; negotiated floors sometimes mid-$20s for sustained commitments.
   - Open-hosts (self-hosted providers we monitor): very wide spread — $6 to $18 / 1M depending on quantization and latency SLOs.

Given your finance target ($7–$12 / 1M), my hypothesis is:
   - To hit $7/1M at scale we will need aggressive quantization + dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated or Private) and a multi-quarter commit.
   - A pragmatic production target in your ramp window is more like ~$10–$15 / 1M assuming modest commit and conservative latency SLOs.

Next steps:
   - I’ll run the parity sheet and return a short one-page recommendation by EOD tomorrow (Friday).
   - Marissa will scope a Dedicated pilot cost estimate if you want us to illustrate committed pricing vs hosted.

If that summary aligns with your recollection, reply with any adjustments. Otherwise we’ll proceed on the above.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: unit price parity review and next steps

Thanks Ben — that looks right. A couple clarifications from our side before you do the parity: 

- The 600M / mo is an expected peak; steady-state for the first 6–9 months will be ~200–300M / mo.
- Latency SLO: 95th pct under 500ms for our chat front-end (user-facing). We can tolerate slightly higher for background batch embeddings.
- We absolutely need an explicit fallback plan if the host model is unavailable; that tradeoff will affect willingness to sign a hard commit.

On the finance side, the $7–$12 / 1M band is their aspirational target. If your recommendation lands at ~$10–$15 / 1M with a clear path to $7 at scale (and a variant with lower latency tradeoffs), we can make a case internally.

Also, can you include an apples-to-apples calc that shows token definitions you're using (input vs output accounting) — some vendors count only input tokens which skews comparisons.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — if you can send the parity by EOD tomorrow that would be perfect.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform, Finlytics
alex.johnson@finlytics.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: unit price parity review and next steps

Perfect — thanks for the clarifications, Alex. Plan for delivery:

1) Parity sheet (attached) — will show per-1M token list price, our expected initial hosted offer, a Dedicated-commit floor, and an Open-host baseline. I will explicitly label token accounting (input+output) and include a second column that shows input-only numbers for fairness to vendors that report that way.
2) Recommended target: we’ll propose an approach with three bands: Pilot (no commit) pricing, Committed (3–12 mo) floors, and Dedicated (reserved capacity) floors. Expect recommended production target ~ $9–$13 / 1M as a pragmatic path given your steady-state volumes; show pathway to <$8 / 1M with Dedicated + quantization + 12-mo commit.
3) SLA/fallback options: two proposals — a fast-response host (slightly higher $/1M) with regional redundancy, and a lower-cost fallback variant (quantized model) for non-critical requests.

I attached the initial parity export (redwood-host-comps-20270429.pdf) and a short volume worksheet derived from your upload. I’ll pull the HubSpot deal into the Recommended Pricing card and flag the options for Marissa to follow up on Dedicated economics if you want to explore commit scenarios.

Deliverable link: https://drive.redwood.com/finlytics/pricing-grid (will update with final files). HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4192/DL-2027-FIN-0192

If that timeline still works we’ll send the finalized parity sheet and a recommended ask language you can use with your procurement team by EOD Friday PST.

Ben
